skill.name: nowait-reasoning-optimizer
skill.description: Implements the NOWAIT technique for efficient reasoning in R1-style LLMs. Use when optimizing inference of reasoning models (QwQ, DeepSeek-R1, Phi4-Reasoning, Qwen3, Kimi-VL, QvQ), reducing chain-of-thought token usage by 27-51% while preserving accuracy. Triggers on "optimize reasoning", "reduce thinking tokens", "efficient inference", "suppress reflection tokens", or when working with verbose CoT outputs.
skill.summary: Reduce reasoning-model output length by suppressing configurable reflection tokens during generation.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Verbose reasoning can increase latency and token costs. This skill applies configurable token suppression to shorten generation while preserving model workflows.
actual_capabilities: Builds suppression token sets from configurable reflection keywords and tokenizer vocabularies.
Applies negative logits to selected token IDs during generation.
Provides bad-word token IDs for compatible inference frameworks.
Offers stopping criteria that limit reflection keyword occurrences.
Includes a convenience function for tokenizing, generating, and decoding optimized responses.
limitations: Effectiveness depends on the model, tokenizer, task, and keyword configuration.
Distilled reasoning models may lose accuracy on difficult tasks.
Substring matching can suppress useful vocabulary unless exclusions are tuned.
The included performance claims are examples and require validation on your workload.

output: Run an unchanged baseline on representative difficult tasks.
Test conservative keyword sets before the complete default list.
Compare accuracy, token count, latency, and truncated answers.
Reject configurations that exceed the defined quality threshold.

best_practices: Measure accuracy and token usage on representative tasks before deployment.
Tune keyword exclusions for each tokenizer and domain.
Keep an unchanged baseline and document every configuration tested.
anti_patterns: Do not assume one keyword list works across every model family.
Do not deploy suppression without checking difficult and safety-sensitive tasks.
Do not treat shorter output as proof of equal reasoning quality.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It reduces selected reflection tokens during reasoning-model generation to target shorter outputs and lower inference overhead.

faq.question: Which frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The included examples cover Hugging Face Transformers and vLLM-compatible bad-word token IDs.

faq.question: Does NOWAIT guarantee lower costs?
faq.answer: No. Savings depend on model behavior, deployment pricing, task complexity, and the selected keyword configuration.

faq.question: Can NOWAIT reduce answer quality?
faq.answer: Yes. Distilled models and difficult tasks may rely on reflection patterns, so benchmark quality before deployment.

faq.question: Can I change the suppression keywords?
faq.answer: Yes. The processor accepts custom keywords and configurable exclusions.

faq.question: Does the skill call external services?
faq.answer: No. Its processor performs local tokenizer and tensor operations, while model acquisition remains the user's separate framework workflow.
